key_insight: Semantic-aware clustering can separate tasks that help each other from tasks that interfere, enabling constructive cooperative multi-task semantic communication.
engineering_relevance: For scientific machine learning systems, this provides a practical way to reduce negative transfer and improve multi-task performance by grouping semantically aligned tasks before joint end-to-end training.
method: Short initial training to extract task representations.
Hierarchical density-based clustering to discover semantically aligned task groups.
End-to-end multi-task semantic communication training performed only within each cluster.
evidence_signal: Simulation results in the abstract report accuracy gains over both unclustered multi-tasking and individual-training baselines.
watch_item: The approach depends on a reliable early semantic representation and a clustering step whose quality may affect downstream grouping and performance.
paper_title: Semantic-Aware Task Clustering for Constructive and Cooperative Multi-Tasking
